output.headline: Epic has the deepest record in the target's own sub-sector on the list, but states it does not acquire: a long-shot call, not a lead.
output.differentiator: Four deals, all in the target's own sub-sector, the most of any buyer on the priority list, and capacity to pay at $6.7B revenue. But it states it makes no acquisitions. [T:record, P:1, P:3]
output.why_them: Deepest own-sub-sector record, but says it does not acquire

acquirer_overview.title: Largest EHR vendor, privately held, and says it does not acquire
points: Privately held since 1979, never took venture capital or private equity; revenue $6.7B (2025, as reported by Forbes), about 14,000 employees. [P:2, P:3, P:4]
Its own site: "We are a software factory (no acquisitions)". A public profile says it has never acquired another company. [P:1, P:2]
The deal file nonetheless lists 4 deals from 2018 to 2022, 3 of 4 closed (75%). That conflicts with its stated position. [T:record, K:closed_share]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Sub-sector fit is real; the stated mandate is the obstacle
points: Share of its deals in the target's sub-sector is the strongest factor in its likelihood; margin fit is a strong factor. [S:sector_share, S:margin_fit]
Technology Capability is the motive in 4 of 4 deals, a tag on only 10% of all deals in the file, so it is a distinct motive. [M:technology_capability]
Having bought in this or a neighbouring region is a modest factor for; having bought from this kind of seller is a modest factor against. [S:geo_fit, S:own_fit_s]

precedent_activity.title: Four Health IT deals from 2018 to 2022, only one near this size
points: Crest Digital Health: $440M Strategic Acquisition, 2022, National, 22.7x EBITDA, closed. [D:MA-2022-0213]
Meridian Health Analytics: $767M Platform Investment, 2018, 22.0x, closed. Oak Clinical Analytics: $15M Merger of Equals, 2021, 18.1x, terminated. [D:MA-2018-0429, D:MA-2021-0372]
Only 1 of 4 deals sits in the comparable size band ($150M-$600M). [K:size_band]

valuation_context.title: Median of 21.4x is the anchor; Epic's own 22.7x sits above it
points: 13 comparable deals, all in the same sub-sector: 19.4x at the 25th percentile, 21.4x median, 23.3x at the 75th. [V:comps]
Target margin of 25.0% is above the comps' median of 22.2% but not in their top quarter, so the 50th percentile is the defensible anchor. [V:comps]
Epic's median paid is 22.7x. Synergy headroom of $14M-$23M and $6.7B revenue mean ability to pay is not the constraint. [V:comps, V:synergy]

risk_flags.title: Stated no-acquisitions policy
risk_flags.concern: Epic's own site says it makes no acquisitions. [R:STATED_NO_ACQUISITIONS]
risk_flags.mitigant: The deal file records 4 deals, 3 closed. [T:record]
risk_flags.reality: The stated policy outweighs the file; the record is not evidence it would buy. [P:1, C:conviction]

risk_flags.title: Execution and recency
risk_flags.concern: One of four deals was terminated, and activity has faded. [D:MA-2021-0372, K:recent]
risk_flags.mitigant: The $440M Crest deal closed in 2022 at 22.7x. [D:MA-2022-0213]
risk_flags.reality: Only 1 deal since 2022 and the last year in the file is 2022. [K:recent, T:record]

risk_flags.title: Competitive process
risk_flags.concern: Other buyers rank higher on the priority list, with similar own-sub-sector records. [N:closest_peers]
risk_flags.mitigant: Epic's 4 own-sub-sector deals exceed Evolent Health's 3. [T:record, N:closest_peers]
risk_flags.reality: Epic would need to change its stated policy before it could compete. [P:1]

conviction.rationale: Capped at Low: Epic states it does not make acquisitions, so its 4 own-sub-sector deals and strongest-factor fit are not evidence it would buy. Treat as a courtesy call, not a lead. [C:conviction, P:1]
